root_cause.text: The MCTP I2C receive function fails to free the allocated skb when the receiver is not allowed (midev->allow_rx is false), causing a skb memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `kfree_skb(skb);` inside the else branch where `midev->allow_rx` is false and `netif_rx()` is not called, and the commit message states "When 'midev->allow_rx' is false, the newly allocated skb isn't consumed by netif_rx(), it needs to free the skb directly."

Releases the lock before freeing the skb, making it impossible to free the skb later in the drop path; the skb remains allocated.

Sets the status to NET_RX_DROP but does not free the skb, contributing to the memory leak as no further cleanup occurs for this path.
Releases the lock before any potential freeing of the skb, making it impossible to free the skb later in the drop path; the skb remains allocated.
This closing brace ends the else block without any kfree_skb call, leaving the skb unfreed and causing a memory leak.
This conditional only handles the success case (NET_RX_SUCCESS); the NET_RX_DROP status set in the else branch is ignored, so no kfree_skb is executed and the skb leaks.

Author: Matt Johnston <matt@codeconstruct.com.au>
Date:   Fri Feb 18 13:51:06 2022 +0800

    mctp i2c: MCTP I2C binding driver
    
    Provides MCTP network transport over an I2C bus, as specified in
    DMTF DSP0237. All messages between nodes are sent as SMBus Block Writes.
    
    Each I2C bus to be used for MCTP is flagged in devicetree by a
    'mctp-controller' property on the bus node. Each flagged bus gets a
    mctpi2cX net device creat
bic_trace_step.reason: In mctp_i2c_recv(), an skb is allocated via netdev_alloc_skb(). When midev->allow_rx is false (lines around 'if (midev->allow_rx)'), the code sets status = NET_RX_DROP and increments rx_dropped, but does not free the skb. This results in a skb memory leak. The fix would require adding a kfree_skb(skb) in the else branch.
